articles.title: iPhone Ultra's cameras might get very unorthodox placement, per leak
articles.summary: A new leak suggests Apple's upcoming foldable iPhone Ultra may place its two front-facing cameras in the corners of the displays rather than the traditional centered position, with one camera on the outer screen and another on the inner screen. If accurate, this would mark a significant departure from Apple's usual iPhone design and could require users to adjust how they take selfies.

articles.title: Instagram introduces a redesigned wordmark
articles.summary: Instagram has introduced a redesigned wordmark for the first time since 2016, giving its name a sharper, more modern look while keeping references to the original style. The new cursive-inspired lettering has received mixed reactions, with some praising the fresher design and others joking that the stylized “r” makes it look like “Instagzam.” Instagram has not said whether the wordmark update will be followed by broader visual changes, such as a new app icon.

articles.title: Here's Your First Look at the Newest Pixel Devices
articles.summary: Google has unveiled its newest Pixel lineup, including Pixel 11 phones, Pixel Watch 5, and its first-ever Pixel Tag finder device. The Pixel 11, 11 Pro, 11 Pro XL, and Pro Fold are built for Gemini Intelligence, with greater durability and upgraded cameras. Pixel Watch 5 adds proactive Gemini features, strength coaching, improved GPS tracking, and Health Guardian tools like breathing emergency detection.

articles.title: AI Governance in Design Tools: What Happens to Your Data When AI Enters the Workflow
articles.summary: AI governance frameworks bring documentation, traceability, and accountability to AI features embedded in design tools. Building a framework involves defining scope and owners, classifying design data, standardizing vendor evaluation, and embedding controls into workflows and CI/CD processes. Penpot positions itself as a governance-friendly alternative through self-hosting, open file formats, and its MCP server, letting organizations control AI models and data flows on their own infrastructure.

articles.title: Measuring Time Savings from Figma Make
articles.summary: Figma's Data Science team ran a randomized controlled trial with 100 participants to measure how much time Figma Make actually saves on design tasks. Design work was found to be 20% faster and 16% easier overall, with product managers seeing the largest gains—23% faster and 37% easier—though designers benefited most on complex tasks while PMs gained more on simpler ones. Figma plans further RCTs, including one testing its new design agent's parallel-agent capabilities.

articles.title: Bias in LLMs, or how to design for everyone with tools built for someone
articles.summary: Large language models are not neutral and often reflect or amplify biases related to language, geography, gender, culture, and socioeconomic status because of the data they are trained on and the feedback systems used to refine them. As a result, AI-generated personas, research summaries, copy, and recommendations can overrepresent dominant groups and present their perspectives as consensus while overlooking minority viewpoints. Designers should treat AI outputs as inputs for further thinking rather than objective conclusions, and actively review them for hidden assumptions, missing perspectives, and demographic bias.

articles.title: Complete Video Editor for macOS (Website)
articles.summary: ShootClip is a complete video editor for macOS — cut, grade, mix, and export with zero learning curve. AI speech-to-text turns every voice into spot-on captions, and the built-in MCP server lets Claude or any AI assistant edit right alongside you.

articles.title: Experiment on Real Products (Website)
articles.summary: Remix lets product and design teams create live variants of the existing app, test them with users, and send the best version to engineering for review.

articles.title: Review Product Changes in the Age of AI (Website)
articles.summary: Agents generate more changes than teams can review. Argos makes every change obvious, then lets your team and your agents comment on the diffs, request updates, or approve before merge.

articles.title: Nine Persona Mistakes that are Costing You Customers
articles.summary: Nine common persona mistakes undermine product design, from over-relying on AI to using outdated, generic, or ignored personas. Personas should be research-based, focused, specific, updated per project, and actively shared across teams to be effective. Avoiding these pitfalls helps teams build products that better match customer needs, improving satisfaction and business outcomes.

articles.title: Got No Time for PRD
articles.summary: PRDs still suit large teams aligning around a known target, but they assume the destination is already chosen, which doesn't fit early exploration. A lighter six-line alternative—Intent, Bet, Bar, Scope, Loop, Never—distills into one sentence short enough to hand directly to an AI agent. Unlike lengthy PRDs models can read but which lock in premature decisions, this compressed brief keeps both humans and agents flexible while testing risky assumptions.

articles.title: Italian Apple Ad Featuring a Toddler With an iPhone Sparks Controversy
articles.summary: Apple is facing criticism and regulatory scrutiny in Italy over a billboard showing a toddler using an iPhone.

articles.title: Playing with scale and perspective, Julie Jonquet-Caunes creates hyperreal renderings of everyday objects
articles.summary: Paris-based illustrator Julie Jonquet-Caunes transforms overlooked everyday objects into meticulous, nostalgic compositions—blending hyperrealist drawing, collage, and art-historical influences to reveal the stories, emotions, and beauty hidden in ordinary details.

articles.title: Everything I Don't Like is Slop
articles.summary: "Slop" has expanded from a label for AI-generated filler into a broader cultural judgment about attention, trust, and creative authenticity.
